threatModel.summary: Jubarte is a Rust document-processing library and CLI with Python/PyO3 and WASM bindings. It compares, reads, edits, validates, repairs, scrubs and renders Word documents using in-memory package/XML processing. Native CLI and Python/Node host adapters supply local filesystem authority; the optional Python MCP adapter exposes document tools over stdio with a persistent directory capability. Rendering additionally uses native host font files and a persistent font index independently of MCP document-root confinement. Optional native self-update downloads GitHub release assets and replaces the executable; maintainer scripts and tag-triggered CI separately publish packages and releases. Representative entry points and gates: src/bin/jubarte.rs:3560-3578, jubarte-python/pyproject.toml:42-49, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,373-381, jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:16-21, src/inspect.rs:604-622, src/convert/mod.rs:769-798, src/update.rs:186-257.
assets: Confidential document text, revision history, comments, embedded media and derived PDF/PNG/Markdown/diff/report outputs; MCP tools return document text, findings and reports as well as output paths to their connected client (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:131-150,185-217,234-255,354-368).

Host filesystem integrity and intended output destinations. Native publication stages bytes beneath each selected output parent; MCP publication instead retains the operator-granted OutputRoot directory handle and accepts only portable relative output names (src/publication.rs:146-225,228-270,420-505).

Source-to-edit binding and the integrity of checked primary output. V1 source SHA-256 checking is conditional on the optional plan field; V2 requires source.sha256 equality. Prepared edits retain source, normalized request and actual chosen-primary digests (src/edit.rs:2081-2089, src/edit/v2_apply.rs:84-99, src/edit/prepared.rs:157-181).

Process availability and memory during ZIP/XML, legacy document, font, image and rendering work. Agent admission defaults are 64 MiB compressed/per-part, 256 MiB total inflated, 10,000 entries and XML depth 256; comparison defaults are 512 MiB compressed/per-part and 2 GiB total inflated with the same entry/depth caps. Overrides replace individual values (src/admission.rs:63-99,103-165).

Native font sources and font-index integrity: JUBARTE_FONT_DIR or platform data folders supply fonts; JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX or the parent of the font folder supplies font-index.tsv. Cached face paths are read by the renderer and the index is persisted through a sibling temporary file and rename (src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652,3098-3107,3154-3172,3213-3229).

Installed executable authenticity and release publication authority. Current self-update trusts GitHub release delivery plus SHA256SUMS.txt; RELEASE_KEYS is empty and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE is None. CI signing secrets, GitHub contents-write credentials and local package-registry credentials are separate authorities (src/update.rs:25-48,198-210,245-257; .github/workflows/release.yml:230-264,278-308,356-369; scripts/release.sh:904-919,929-958,1063-1069).
trustBoundaries: Untrusted DOCX/ZIP/XML bytes cross into package admission and then DOM/document operations. Opened::open admits using default limits, normalizes Strict packages and opens/parses within those limits. General rendering calls admit_package before package/DOM construction. The common archive opener rejects reported structural defects, while the deliberately unchecked opener supports triage and admission's own typed checks (src/inspect.rs:604-622; src/convert/mod.rs:769-798; src/opc/archive.rs:15-51).

Raw XML library callers choose between checked and permissive APIs. try_parse_xdocument_with_limits validates before constructing the DOM; parse_xdocument explicitly requires a prior gate and does not enforce input policy itself. Shared defaults include 1,024 element attributes, 1,024 attribute-name bytes, 64 MiB attribute values and 128 MiB start tags (src/xmllinq/parse.rs:25-36,48-57,91-98,119-135).

Edit requests cross from caller-authored plans to document mutations. V1 checks a supplied source hash, refuses blank authors and signed/macro-bearing inputs; V2 requires the exact source hash and resolves scope/context before operations. These are document-consistency controls, not user authentication or authorization (src/edit.rs:2072-2105; src/edit/v2_apply.rs:84-110). Dry run and application share in-memory preparation; filesystem publication remains a separate host operation (src/edit/prepared.rs:5-13,157-186).

Native CLI users grant ambient authority through selected input/output paths. publish_paths opens and retains each actual parent rather than enforcing a global document root; staging uses an exclusive UUID directory and file, with Unix staging directory mode 0700. Publication is atomic per file and records partial commits/durability uncertainty rather than promising set-wide rollback (src/publication.rs:5-7,83-143,203-225,420-505).

The MCP connected client can invoke registered read and write tools within the root chosen by the server operator. Startup defaults --root to cwd, resolves it once and serves stdio. Python containment checks are preliminary diagnostics; actual document reads and output publication pass through native _OutputRoot and cap-std directory-relative operations. No per-tool user identity or tenant separation is established; tool annotations are hints, while OutputRoot owns filesystem confinement (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,67-108,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1276; src/publication.rs:146-199).

Native font discovery/cache is a separate authority from document-root publication. Font-family lookup can inspect system, Word, cloud and configured user-font directories; cloud family names must be one normal path component. The index may read cached face paths and write its configured file outside the MCP root. Its enforcing boundary is host environment/filesystem authority, not OutputRoot (src/convert/font.rs:2225-2236,2263-2315,2633-2652,2855-2862,3098-3107,3154-3172,3213-3229).

WASM byte APIs do not receive native publication::OutputRoot because that module is compiled only outside wasm32. Python and WASM bindings disable engine default features and request only cli grammar, so optional self-update is not part of those engine dependencies. Node's separately shipped CLI grants ambient filesystem access through node:fs around the WASM engine; its read/write helpers are distinct from native staged publication (src/lib.rs:147-149,163-165; jubarte-python/Cargo.toml:35-39; jubarte-wasm/Cargo.toml:18-23; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:16-21,52-79,106-111).

Self-update is an explicit native CLI capability. It selects fixed jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines repository, platform archive and inner binary path; requests checksum verification and regular-file verification; prompts unless --yes, and --check does not install. Current keys leave signature verification disabled. Dependency-owned download, archive extraction and executable-swap behavior is not established merely by this wrapper (src/bin/jubarte.rs:3892-3896,4062-4073; src/update.rs:25-48,186-257,274-285,299-321).

Release publication is privileged operator/CI work, separate from document processing. CI triggers on v* tags, checks tag/package version, grants build jobs contents:read and release job contents:write, optionally signs assets with step-scoped ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY, then publishes dist/* using step-scoped GH_TOKEN. Local release script has packaging dry runs and version confirmation unless YES, then separately publishes crates.io, two npm packages and PyPI with configured credentials (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,31-49,230-264,278-308,317-322,356-369; scripts/release.sh:729-747,874-888,904-919,929-958,1039-1069).
attackerCapabilities: A document supplier controls package names, relationships, XML, revision/comment content, embedded fonts/images and document complexity submitted to a consumer. This does not imply host configuration, MCP root directory, registry accounts or release asset access (src/admission.rs:13-28; SECURITY.md:36-78).

A connected MCP client can request supported reads/mutations under operator-selected root and overwrite=true. Tools expose that shared root capability, not a separate tenant identity. Escape would add host access not granted (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,152-168,258-277,373-381).

An edit-plan author controls operations and V1 source-hash inclusion. Author strings and revision metadata are document data rather than authenticated identities. Consistency guards are not authorization (src/edit.rs:2081-2105; src/edit/v2_apply.rs:84-110).

A malicious local peer may possess filesystem access to writable output/cache directories depending on deployment; this is conditional, not assumed. Native held handles, exclusive staging and MCP path validation are relevant to races when such a peer exists (src/publication.rs:146-148,228-270,420-505).

Control of GitHub release assets, signing material or registry accounts is a conditional supply-chain starting capability, not ordinary document input. Current checksum-only update authenticity depends on release authority and transport/dependency controls; distinct signing-key compromise is not required because trusted keys are empty (src/update.rs:25-48,198-210,245-257; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-82).
securityObjectives: Refuse packages/XML violating active policy before unbounded downstream parsing; caller owns process memory/CPU limits and permissive raw XML API obligations (src/admission.rs:13-28,63-99; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:25-36,119-135; SECURITY.md:72-78).

Keep relationships within package semantics and preserve external targets as data rather than retrieval authority. Representative comparison treats External targets as strings and reads internal part bytes (src/document_comparer.rs:94-108). Broader no-network guarantee requires checking all consumers.

Keep MCP document reads and explicit artifact writes beneath retained root, refusing escape symlinks, unsafe names and unrequested overwrite; distinguish ambient renderer font/cache I/O (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108; src/publication.rs:146-199,228-270,448-464; src/convert/font.rs:3098-3107,3213-3229).

Bind verification/receipt digests to chosen primary bytes and report refused plans without publication. V1 snapshot binding is optional when source_sha256 absent (src/edit/prepared.rs:5-13,157-186; src/edit.rs:2081-2089).

Preserve existing native outputs on staging failure, commit complete bytes per file and report prior commits on later failure; no all-files atomic transaction is promised (src/publication.rs:83-143,168-174,420-505).

Executable replacement requires explicit update and configured release/checksum/regular-file controls; implemented signature support differs from current checksum-only configuration (src/update.rs:44-48,186-257,299-321).

Keep document clients separate from maintainer credentials/signing keys; bind CI releases to v* tag and matching package version with scoped permissions/checksums (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,31-49,230-264,317-322,356-369).

findings.title: Python and npm CLIs can overwrite unrelated files through output and staging symlinks
findings.summary: Both filesystem CLI adapters check whether an output exists, then open its pathname for a truncating write. They also record edit plans through predictable PID-named partial files opened without exclusive creation. A local attacker who can write the selected output/plan directory can redirect these writes to another file writable by the victim process. Ordinary output redirection requires a race when the referent exists; plan partial-file planting can be done before its write. This affects Python and npm CLI paths, while native publication and MCP use separate controls.

severity.rationale: Medium integrity impact with medium likelihood: this is a local shared-directory attack requiring victim CLI execution in an attacker-writable directory, plus successful name replacement or prediction/observation of the PID-based staging name. No remote exposure or privileged execution is established.
severity.changeConditions: Higher impact requires a victim with greater filesystem privileges and an exploitable writable target; private non-writable output directories remove the attacker prerequisite.

confidence.rationale: Source directly shows nonexclusive, symlink-following writes after preflight and predictable plan staging in both adapters; platform behavior was assessed statically, with no exploit executed.

codeEvidence.explanation: The pathname is checked independently of the write; a dangling symlink also appears absent.

codeEvidence.label: npm sink truncates the path it opens
codeEvidence.explanation: Default writeFileSync flags follow a substituted symlink and truncate its writable referent.

codeEvidence.label: npm plan staging is predictable and nonexclusive
codeEvidence.explanation: A planted partial-file link is followed before rename, corrupting the referent even though the final step renames a link.

codeEvidence.label: Python output sink follows pathname links
codeEvidence.explanation: The separate exists check is not an atomic authorization of the opened file.

codeEvidence.label: Python plan staging repeats the same flaw
codeEvidence.code:
target = Path(os.path.realpath(plan))
        partial = target.with_name(f".{target.name}.{os.getpid()}.partial")
        try:
            partial.write_bytes(recorded["json"].encode("utf-8"))

codeEvidence.explanation: Resolving the intended plan target does not protect the newly derived partial pathname.

rootCause.summary: Filesystem adapters implement output authorization as pathname preflight followed by ordinary truncating writes, and create predictable staging files without exclusive/no-follow semantics. They bypass the hardened native publication mechanism.

findings.remediation: Route Python and npm output, bundle, report and plan publication through a shared safe publisher: hold the destination directory, stage into exclusively created private storage, never follow staging symlinks, and install with atomic no-clobber semantics unless overwrite was explicitly requested. For intentional plan-symlink targets, resolve the authorized target first, then use exclusive staging beside it.

counterEvidence: The local attacker must have write access to the actual selected directory. Ordinary authorized --force behavior alone is not a vulnerability.
recordPlan/_record intentionally resolve an explicitly selected plan symlink; the independently attacker-planted partial symlink is the vulnerability.
src/publication.rs:472-505,558-569 hardens native publication; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:101-108 delegates to confined native publication. These are separate paths.
limitations: No live filesystem race or privileged victim scenario was reproduced.
validation.method: Offline source tracing; no runtime execution
validation.summary: Parent verified both output helpers, plan-recording entrypoints and staging sinks. The plan is previewed but that controls edit validity, not the filesystem object opened. Native publication uses UUID private staging, create_new and no-clobber hard links; MCP uses that separate OutputRoot, so neither mitigates these CLI adapter sinks.

controls: Private output directories deny the necessary directory mutation. Native/MCP publishers are independently hardened.

dataflow.summary: Attacker-controlled directory entries replace the CLI output after exists preflight, or precreate .<plan>.<pid>.partial. writeFileSync/write_bytes follows the link with victim privileges, writes generated bytes to the referent, then plan recording renames the partial pathname.

attackPath.likelihood: Conditional local attack; no remote or default shared deployment asserted.

findings.title: HTML altChunk colspan permits unbounded markup expansion during rendering
findings.summary: A small admitted DOCX can contain an internal HTML/MHT altChunk with a very large td/th colspan. The converter parses this value as usize and emits one w:gridCol element per claimed column, without a semantic count or generated-output budget. For example, a span of 1,000,000,000 entails a billion formatting iterations and tens of gigabytes of generated XML before DOM parsing, exhausting the rendering process.

severity.rationale: Process availability impact is medium and likelihood is high once an untrusted document is rendered: a tiny integer attribute drives immediate deterministic unbounded work. No remote service deployment is assumed.
severity.changeConditions: A shared conversion service increases operational impact. Strict external process memory/CPU limits contain host-wide impact but still allow the input to terminate its conversion worker.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified the admitted-byte entrypoint, internal relationship loading, usize parsing and per-column emission loop. No material source reachability blocker; no runtime payload executed.

codeEvidence.label: HTML colspan has only a lower bound
codeEvidence.explanation: A small decimal attribute can denote far more columns than any admission byte/depth bound.

codeEvidence.label: Each claimed column creates XML text
codeEvidence.explanation: cols is the maximum unchecked per-row sum of spans (469-475). The output String grows once per claimed column.

codeEvidence.label: Expansion runs after original package admission
codeEvidence.explanation: Admission at 773 validates original ZIP/XML, not the expansion before this String is constructed.

rootCause.summary: The HTML importer treats document-supplied colspan as a trusted expansion count. It sums spans and serializes a physical XML column for every claimed slot without checking a maximum or generated byte budget.

findings.remediation: Refuse out-of-range HTML column spans before adding cells; use checked cumulative grid accounting and a small documented maximum column count. Carry a generated-markup/resource budget into altChunk expansion and return a typed refusal before allocating or iterating over excessive derived content.

counterEvidence: Archive compressed/inflated-byte, entry, XML depth and tag limits exist; the input with one short HTML attribute fits those limits.
The chunk loader only looks up pkg.part_bytes using the resolved relationship path (src/convert/mod.rs:790-793,21301-21304); it performs no network request. The finding uses an internal HTML part.
SECURITY.md recommends CPU/memory-constrained processes and disclaims universal denial-of-service protection; these contain consequences but do not bound the expansion.
limitations: No runtime reproduction or deployment-specific concurrency impact measured.
validation.summary: Static trace confirms render/docx_to_pdf enter with_layout, admit the original package, load the internal chunk, parse an arbitrary usize span, and loop cols times in end_table. No schema validator or semantic span limit intervenes; a one-billion-column span fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize.

controls: Original archive and XML limits apply before conversion.
External process resource limits can contain impact.

dataflow.summary: Attacker supplies DOCX main XML containing w:altChunk with an internal relationship to an HTML/MHT part -> with_layout -> altchunk::expand -> html_to_wml -> Builder::start parses td/th colspan -> Builder::end_table sums spans -> billion-iteration String generation before DOM parse.

attackPath.impact: Excess CPU work and memory allocation can terminate or stall the conversion process.

reachability.summary: Public Rust PDF/render APIs and Python/WASM wrappers accept document bytes. A normal table in an internal HTML altChunk reaches this path after admission; no special host setting or raised input limits are required.
reachability.attacker: Provider of an untrusted document rendered by a victim/library consumer
preconditions: Victim renders attacker-supplied DOCX containing an internal HTML/MHT altChunk.

remediationTests: Use a tiny in-memory altChunk HTML with excessive td/th colspan and assert a prompt typed refusal without output growth.
Exercise cumulative spans across multiple cells, numeric overflow and valid inclusive limits.

findings.title: ZIP footer interpretation mismatch bypasses the entry-count budget
findings.summary: The preindex guard checks an independently parsed EOCD total-entry count, while zip9.0.5 uses the ZIP32 per-disk count to construct its index. No actual-count cap repairs the mismatch after opening.

severity.rationale: Medium availability impact with high likelihood of bypassing an explicit configured entry budget. Compressed/inflated byte limits still constrain the archive, so this is not unlimited host-resource control or proof of remote exposure.
severity.changeConditions: Shared in-process deployments may suffer broader availability loss; external process resource limits contain host impact but still permit worker termination.
